title: pricing-packaging-back-of-envelope-notes-ethan-2026-03-04
body:
Notes to self — quick unit econ + tier ideas (scratchpad)

Context / goal:
- Fast back-of-envelope to sanity-check per-token economics for hosted API (open-ish 13B quantized family) and rough tiering.
- Want simple public pricing that (a) covers cost + margin, (b) differentiates reserved/dedicated contracts, and (c) aligns with PLG motion.

Assumptions (rough):
- Model: open-13B quantized (q4 family) used for majority of traffic.
- Infra compute cost (amortized per-token on GPUs + spot infra): ~0.0000025 USD/token (compute-only) — derived from avg throughput + instance amortization.
- Platform overhead (routing, cache, KV, monitoring, storage egress) ~40% of compute => +0.0000010
- Ops/SRE/support amortized on usage => +0.0000015
- Total fully-loaded cost per token (C) ~= 0.000005 USD/token.

Sanity-check numbers:
- Per-1k-token cost = C * 1000 = $0.005 (half a cent).
- Target gross margin (hosted, self-serve) 60–75% => list price target per 1k tokens: $0.0125–$0.02.
- Use a single conservative list point for drafts: $0.015 / 1k tokens (fits mid-range).

Example request economics (avg request):
- Avg tokens (input+output): 500 tokens/request (30 input / 470 output is a common chat pattern).
- Cost per request = 500 * C = $0.0025 (0.25c).
- Revenue per request at $0.015/1k = 0.5 * $0.015 = $0.0075 => margin ~67% (ok).

Volume scenarios (monthly):
- Small app: 10M tokens/mo => cost = 10,000 * $0.005 = $50; revenue = 10,000 * $0.015 = $150 => GBP (gross profit) $100/mo.
- Scale app: 100M tokens/mo => cost = $500; revenue = $1500 => GP $1000/mo.
- Big: 1B tokens/mo => cost = $5,000; revenue = $15,000 => GP $10,000 (still healthy).

Implications + quick notes:
- The per-token cost is sensitive to model choice and quantization. If customers switch to larger models (70B) cost can be 3–5x; pricing should reflect model family (price multiplier).
- Embeddings: different cost profile (mostly forward pass, fewer tokens). Quick stub: $0.004 per 1k embedding tokens (or $0.0005 per vector) — need proper measurement.
- Minimums: for tiny customers, billing granularity and monthly minimums matter more than per-token price. Consider $5/mo starter credit for free-tier conversion.

Draft tier ideas (hosted API):
1) Free / Developer
   - 0–100k tokens/mo free (trial + dev).
   - Rate-limited, lower priority, no SLA.
2) Starter (self-serve) 
   - $10/mo + $0.02 per 1k tokens OR $0.015 per 1k tokens billed usage-only (we can A/B).
   - 0–50M tokens range for typical startups.
   - Includes basic dashboards, 7-day logs.
3) Scale (growing products)
   - $0.01–$0.012 per 1k tokens (volume tiers: 50M–1B).
   - Longer retention, higher rate limits, basic SSO.
4) Enterprise / Dedicated
   - Reserved capacity pricing (commitments). e.g., Dedicated GPU pool pricing: $X per GPU-hour reserved + $0.004 per 1k tokens for overflow usage (numbers need ops validation).
   - SLA, VPC, audit logs, KMS.

Bundling / packaging levers:
- Model family multipliers: e.g., base price for 13B = 1x, 70B = 3x, instruction-tuned high-cost variants = 4x.
- API feature tiers (streaming, function-calling, tool calling) can be same price but gating quotas for free/starter.
- Cached KV / prefix caching discounts: for high cache-hit workloads, provide negotiated discounts since effective cost is lower.

Thoughts on reserved / Dedicated pricing (ballpark):
- Simple approach: per-GPU-hour reservation fee + nominal per-token for overflow. Example anchor: $4–$12 per GPU-hour depends on infra (this needs infra team input).
- Offer commit bands: 1–4 GPUs, 5–16 GPUs, 16+ GPUs with step-down pricing.
- Also offer a QPS/latency-backed SLA with overage pricing if commit exceeded.

Open questions / to validate with infra/ops:
- Actual amortized compute cost per token by model family (13B / 33B / 70B) with quantized kernels — need measured numbers from serving-runtime.
- Storage/embedding indexing cost for vector DBs (we should model embedding inference + search overhead).
- Customer acquisition patterns: do most convert at Starter ($10/mo) or go straight to usage-only? Historical GA data helpful.
- Competitive pricing points (OpenAI, Cohere, Anthropic) — quick comp table needed.

Next steps (actionable):
- Ping @Maya to get measured per-token cost by model family (deep breakdown: compute / infra / ops).
- Draft a simple public pricing page mock with the three hosted tiers + enterprise contact.
- Prepare an internal calc sheet (per-tenant revenue/cost model) to simulate break-even for different churn/usage patterns.

Notes to self: keep public numbers simple (2–3 price points). Use reserved/dedicated as enterprise negotiation territory. Document assumptions clearly so we can change list prices once infra numbers land.

-- end scratchpad --
